facts.basis: Fifteenth Finance Commission award. Paid only to the states the Commission assessed as still in deficit after devolution — a named and shrinking list, which is why most states receive nothing under this head.

facts.notes: The nineteen states absent from the state list received nothing under this head in 2024-25. The grant exists to close an assessed revenue gap remaining after devolution, so a state leaves the list once the Commission judged that gap closed — Karnataka's entitlement ended after 2021-22, Kerala's and Andhra Pradesh's after 2023-24.

facts.basis: Fifteenth Finance Commission award. State-wise amounts fixed from each state's past disaster expenditure and its exposure to risk.

cite.locator: Demand No. 42, item 3, Actual 2024-25

facts.basis: Follows the projects themselves. External assistance is passed to a state on the same terms the union received it from the donor — so it goes wherever the funded project is, not by any formula. North-eastern and Himalayan states are outside this back-to-back arrangement.

facts.basis: Fifteenth Finance Commission award. Allocated by the Commission's health-sector formula.

facts.basis: Follows the projects themselves, as with the loan component — determined by which state hosts the donor-funded project.

cite.locator: Demand No. 42, item 12, Actual 2024-25

facts.basis: Fifteenth Finance Commission award. State-wise amounts fixed in the award, as for the response fund.

cite.locator: Demand No. 42, item 4, Actual 2024-25

facts.basis: Discretionary. The demand describes it as covering committed liabilities without provision and other need-based assistance, so it is decided case by case rather than by any published rule.

cite.locator: Demand No. 42, item 9, Actual 2024-25

facts.basis: Event-driven. Released to a state after a notified disaster, against assessed need, so it depends on what happened that year rather than on any share.

cite.locator: Demand No. 42, item 15, Actual 2024-25, net

facts.basis: Not a transfer to any state. It is the union topping up the national disaster funds beyond what the National Calamity Contingent Duty covers.
